He moved to California in 1995 to attend [Stanford University](Stanford_University "Stanford University"). However, Musk dropped out after two days and, with his brother [Kimbal](Kimbal_Musk "Kimbal Musk"), co-founded online [city guide](City_guide "City guide") software company <Zip2>. The startup was acquired by <Compaq> for $307 million in 1999, and with $12 million of the money he made, that same year Musk co-founded [X.com](X.com_(bank) "X.com (bank)"), a [direct bank](Direct_bank "Direct bank"). In 2002, [eBay](EBay "EBay") acquired PayPal for $1.5 billion, and that same year, with $100 million of the money he made, Musk founded SpaceX, a [spaceflight](Spaceflight "Spaceflight") services company. He became its chairman and product architect, assuming the position of CEO in 2008. In 2006, Musk helped create <SolarCity>, a solar-energy company that was acquired by Tesla in 2016 and became [Tesla Energy](Tesla_Energy "Tesla Energy"). In 2013, he proposed a [hyperloop](Hyperloop "Hyperloop") high-speed [vactrain](Vactrain "Vactrain") transportation system. [Musk has expressed views](Views_of_Elon_Musk "Views of Elon Musk") that have made him a polarizing figure. In 2018, the [U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission](U.S._Securities_and_Exchange_Commission "U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission") (SEC) sued him for falsely tweeting that he had secured funding for a private takeover of Tesla. The Model 3 is the all-time bestselling plug-in electric car worldwide, and in June 2021 it became the first electric car to sell 1 million units globally.[[120]](Elon_Musk#cite_note-1miModel3-123)[[121]](Elon_Musk#cite_note-Model3TopEV-124) A fifth vehicle, the [Model Y](Tesla_Model_Y "Tesla Model Y") crossover, was launched in 2020.[[122]](Elon_Musk#cite_note-125) The [Cybertruck](Tesla_Cybertruck "Tesla Cybertruck"), an all-electric pickup truck, was unveiled in 2019.[[123]](Elon_Musk#cite_note-126) Under Musk, Tesla has also constructed multiple lithium-ion battery and electric vehicle factories, named [Gigafactories](Gigafactory "Gigafactory").[[124]](Elon_Musk#cite_note-127)

Since its [initial public offering](Initial_public_offering "Initial public offering") in 2010,[[125]](Elon_Musk#cite_note-128) Tesla stock has risen significantly; it became the most valuable carmaker in summer 2020,[[126]](Elon_Musk#cite_note-129)[[127]](Elon_Musk#cite_note-130) and it entered the [S&P 500](S%26P_500 "S&P 500") later that year.[[128]](Elon_Musk#cite_note-131)[[129]](Elon_Musk#cite_note-132) In October 2021, it reached a market capitalization of $1 trillion, the sixth company in U.S. history to do so.[[130]](Elon_Musk#cite_note-133) In November 2021, Musk proposed, on <Twitter>, to sell 10% of his Tesla stock, since "much is made lately of unrealized gains being a means of tax avoidance".[[131]](Elon_Musk#cite_note-Haselton-2021-134) After more than 3.5 million Twitter accounts supported the sale, Musk sold $6.9 billion of Tesla stock within a week,[[131]](Elon_Musk#cite_note-Haselton-2021-134) and a total of $16.4 billion by year end, reaching the 10% target.[[132]](Elon_Musk#cite_note-135) In February 2022, *[The Wall Street Journal](The_Wall_Street_Journal "The Wall Street Journal")* reported that both Elon and Kimbal Musk were under investigation by the SEC for possible insider trading related to the sale.[[133]](Elon_Musk#cite_note-136) In 2022, Musk unveiled a robot developed by Tesla, [Optimus](Optimus_(robot) "Optimus (robot)").[[134]](Elon_Musk#cite_note-137) On June 20, 2023, Musk met with [Indian Prime Minister](Prime_minister_of_India "Prime minister of India") [Narendra Modi](Narendra_Modi "Narendra Modi") in [New York City](Indians_in_the_New_York_City_metropolitan_area "Indians in the New York City metropolitan area"), suggesting that he might be interested in investing in India "as soon as humanly possible".[[135]](Elon_Musk#cite_note-ModiNewYorkCity-138)

#### SEC and shareholder lawsuits regarding tweets

In 2018, Musk was [sued](Tesla%2C_Inc.#Lawsuits_and_controversies "Tesla, Inc.") by the SEC for a [tweet](Tweeted "Tweeted") claiming that funding had been secured for potentially taking Tesla private.[[136]](Elon_Musk#cite_note-Goldstein_27-9-18-139)[[lower-alpha 4]](Elon_Musk#cite_note-143) The lawsuit characterized the tweet as false, misleading, and damaging to investors, and sought to bar Musk from serving as CEO of [publicly traded companies](Public_company "Public company").[[136]](Elon_Musk#cite_note-Goldstein_27-9-18-139)[[140]](Elon_Musk#cite_note-144)[[141]](Elon_Musk#cite_note-OkaneLopatto18-145) Two days later, Musk settled with the SEC, without admitting or denying the SEC's allegations. As a result, Musk and Tesla were fined $20 million each, and Musk was forced to step down for three years as Tesla chairman but was able to remain as CEO.[[142]](Elon_Musk#cite_note-146) Musk has stated in interviews that he does not regret posting the tweet that triggered the SEC investigation.[[143]](Elon_Musk#cite_note-147)[[144]](Elon_Musk#cite_note-148) In April 2022, the shareholder who sued Musk over the tweet, along with several Tesla shareholders, said that a federal judge had ruled that the tweet was false, although the ruling in question has not been unsealed.[[145]](Elon_Musk#cite_note-149) In February 2023, the jury found Musk and Tesla not liable.[[146]](Elon_Musk#cite_note-150)

In 2019, Musk stated in a tweet that Tesla would build half a million cars that year.[[147]](Elon_Musk#cite_note-151) The SEC reacted to Musk's tweet by filing in court, asking the court to hold him in contempt for violating the terms of a settlement agreement with such a tweet; the accusation was disputed by Musk. #### SolarCity and Tesla Energy

Musk provided the initial concept and financial capital for <SolarCity>, which his cousins [Lyndon](Lyndon_Rive "Lyndon Rive") and Peter Rive founded in 2006.[[153]](Elon_Musk#cite_note-157) By 2013, SolarCity was the second largest provider of solar power systems in the United States.[[154]](Elon_Musk#cite_note-158) In 2014, Musk promoted the idea of SolarCity building an advanced production facility in [Buffalo](Buffalo%2C_New_York "Buffalo, New York"), [New York](New_York_(state) "New York (state)"), triple the size of the largest solar plant in the United States.[[155]](Elon_Musk#cite_note-159) Construction of the [factory](Gigafactory_2 "Gigafactory 2") started in 2014 and was completed in 2017. It operated as a joint venture with <Panasonic> until early 2020.[[156]](Elon_Musk#cite_note-160)[[157]](Elon_Musk#cite_note-161)

Tesla acquired SolarCity for over $2 billion in 2016 and merged it with its battery unit to create [Tesla Energy](Tesla_Energy "Tesla Energy"). At the time, SolarCity was facing liquidity issues.[[158]](Elon_Musk#cite_note-162) Multiple shareholder groups filed a lawsuit against Musk and Tesla's directors, claiming that the purchase of SolarCity was done solely to benefit Musk and came at the expense of Tesla and its shareholders.[[159]](Elon_Musk#cite_note-163)[[160]](Elon_Musk#cite_note-164) Tesla directors settled the lawsuit in January 2020, leaving Musk the sole remaining defendant.[[161]](Elon_Musk#cite_note-165)[[162]](Elon_Musk#cite_note-166) Two years later, the court ruled in Musk's favor.[[163]](Elon_Musk#cite_note-167)

In 2017, Musk founded the Boring Company to construct tunnels, and revealed plans for specialized, underground, high-occupancy vehicles that could travel up to 150 miles per hour (240 km/h) and thus circumvent above-ground traffic in major cities.[[176]](Elon_Musk#cite_note-180)[[177]](Elon_Musk#cite_note-cnndogecoin-181) Early in 2017, the company began discussions with [regulatory bodies](Regulatory_agency "Regulatory agency") and initiated construction of a 30-foot (9.1 m) wide, 50-foot (15 m) long, and 15-foot (4.6 m) deep "test trench" on the premises of SpaceX's offices, as that required no permits.[[178]](Elon_Musk#cite_note-boring-182) The [Los Angeles tunnel](Boring_Test_Tunnel "Boring Test Tunnel"), less than two miles (3.2 km) in length, debuted to journalists in 2018. ### Twitter / X

You are a helpful assistant. Current date: 11-20-2023.

# Multi-Agent Delegation

When the user asks a complex question, do not attempt to answer it yourself. Break it up into smaller pieces, then use the `fork` tool to delegate each piece to a subagent. You MUST use the `join` tool to retrieve the subagent's result for each subagent you create with `fork`. Each subagent has access to the exact same tools that you do.

If you are confident you can answer the user's query without help, do not use the delegation tools.
